In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of grazyme B is a marker of CTL activation and is associated with HIV infection, but does not necessarily imply that the cytotoxic T cells are killing their targets.

granzyme B is a good marker for CTL activity, and that the increase in the percentage and absolute number of granzyme-positive cells in HIV infection reflects the large increase of CTL activity in the lymphoid tissue of HIV-infected subjects, which is a consequence of the massive activation and expansion of CTLs in the course of HIV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV infection leads to a massive influx of CD8 T cells in the lymph nodes, which is associated with an increase in granzyme B expression by these cells.
HIV infection leads to a profound alteration in lymphoid architecture.
the destruction of the germ centers during HIV infection is caused by cytotoxic T cells, which are present in relatively large numbers from early stages of HIV disease onward.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the lymphoid tissue of HIV-infected individuals is characterized by a massive accumulation of cytotoxic CD8+ T cell, which is present in both the germ center and the inter-follicular areas of the lymph node.
HIV infection is a systemic disease that affects the entire lymphoid system.

the CD8+ cells that infiltrate the lymph nodes during the course of HIV infection are killing competent, and that the destruction of the lymphoid microenvironment is likely to be mediated by these cells.
